subject.title: [优化建议] install.sh 模块化拆分以提升可维护性

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a modular `scripts/install.sh` source layout now, and should the public served installer remain a generated single-file artifact?
rationale: The request is plausible maintainability work on a stable setup surface, but current docs, tests, and website sync assume one directly served shell script, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term artifact strategy.

options.title: Sponsor a generated-artifact split
options.body: Approve a modular source layout only if it still publishes one tested `openclaw.ai/install.sh` artifact and updates the installer validation matrix in the same change.

options.title: Allow only bug-tied extractions
options.body: Use this issue as backlog context and extract installer sections only when doing concrete bug fixes or validation improvements that already need that boundary.

options.title: Keep the installer monolithic
options.body: Decide that the shell installer should stay single-file to minimize helper-loading and website-publishing risk.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a generated-artifact split
recommendation.body: Approve a modular source layout only if it still publishes one tested `openclaw.ai/install.sh` artifact and updates the installer validation matrix in the same change.

likelyOwner.reason: Current installer blame, website-sync ownership, and package-manager installer PR history make this the strongest available routing signal for the artifact strategy decision.
